Each phrase speaks in a native Kannada voice. Slow it to 0.2× and repeat until it sticks.

hfaqs.a: No. Start with spoken Kannada in Roman letters, and let the script come second. Learners who speak first stay motivated far longer than learners who drill letters for a month before saying a word.
hfaqs.q: Must I learn the Kannada script before speaking?

hfaqs.a: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ for respect, ಹೌದು and ಇಲ್ಲ, ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು, ಸರಿ, and ನಾನು — I. With those seven you can open any interaction in Karnataka politely while your vocabulary grows underneath.
hfaqs.q: Which words should I learn in week one?

hfaqs.a: The retroflex family new to most ears — ಳ, ಣ, long-short vowel pairs, rolled ರ. Ten minutes of daily listening retunes your ears within weeks; the pronunciation page walks you through each one.
hfaqs.q: What is the hardest part of Kannada?

topics.desc: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ opens every door in Karnataka — plus mornings, welcomes and warm goodbyes. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Yes, and nobody will mind — ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ with folded hands is understood and loved everywhere Kannada is spoken. With close friends a smile and ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ? (are you well?) feels warmer.
faqs.q: Can I just say namaskaara everywhere?

faqs.a: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ with folded hands and a small nod, and ನೀವು (neevu — formal you) until invited closer. Add ಅಣ್ಣ (anna) or ಅಕ್ಕ (akka) for someone slightly older — it warms everything instantly.
faqs.q: How do I greet an elder respectfully?

faqs.a: ಮತ್ತೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ (matte sigona — we'll meet again) is the warm standard. ಹೋಗಿ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ (hogi barteeni — I'll go and come back) is the classic respectful farewell — receive it with a smile and a nod.
faqs.q: How do Kannada people say goodbye?

topics.note: A note on ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ vs ಆರಾಮಿದ್ದೀರಾ. ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ? (chennaagiddeeraa) is the everyday are you well? — warm, quick, everywhere. ಆರಾಮಿದ್ದೀರಾ? is its relaxed elder cousin, heard over filter coffee. Start with ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ; the rest arrives with ajjis.
paras: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ (namaskaara) is the one greeting that never fails. Folded hands, a small nod, and it works with strangers, elders, shopkeepers and officials — exactly the people a learner meets first. Say it clearly, hold the folded hands half a second, and Karnataka opens to you.

Mornings get their own greeting: ಶುಭೋದಯ (shubhodaya — good morning), heard in offices, schools and darshinis until about eleven. Evenings soften to ಶುಭಸಂಜೆ (shubhasanje). Time-stamped greetings signal that you live in the language, not just visit it.

Welcomes are grand in Kannada culture: ಸ್ವಾಗತ (svaagata — welcome) opens homes, shops and hearts. Guests are greeted standing, often with water or coffee before a single question. Return the warmth — ಬಂದೆ, ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (I've come, thank you) — and you are family within minutes.

Goodbyes promise return, never end: ಮತ್ತೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ (we'll meet again) is the everyday farewell; ಜಾಗ್ರತೆ (jaagrate — take care) adds affection. Leave every conversation with a ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ and a smile — in Karnataka, how you leave is remembered longer than how you came.

topics.desc: Vowels, consonants, ottaksharas and the curly ಳ — the Kannada alphabet without tears. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Thirteen vowels (ಸ್ವರಗಳು) and thirty-four consonants (ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳು) — 47+ letters that combine into ottaksharas. Sounds huge, behaves simply: learn the shapes and the combinations assemble themselves.
faqs.q: How many letters does Kannada have?

faqs.a: ಳ (lla) — the retroflex liquid, curled back: ಬೆಳಕು, ಕಳಸ. Then the ottaksharalu stacks — ಕ್ಷ, ಜ್ಞ, ತ್ರ. Listen, curl, practise: they arrive within weeks.
faqs.q: What is the hardest Kannada letter?

faqs.a: Yes — in writing: ಖ ಘ ಛ ಝ ಠ ಢ ಥ ಧ ಫ ಭ appear in Sanskrit loans (ಕ್ಷಮೆ, ಧರ್ಮ). Daily Kannada softens most of them; recognise them in print, relax in speech.
faqs.q: Does Kannada have kh, gh, bh sounds?

topics.note: A note on ಒತ್ತಕ್ಷರ (ottakshara). Kannada stacks consonants into ottaksharas: ಕ್ + ಷ = ಕ್ಷ, ಜ್ + ಞ = ಜ್ಞ. The second consonant tucks underneath the first — once you see the pattern, stacked letters read themselves. One look down, and the whole conjunct system clicks.
paras: Kannada vowels (ಸ್ವರಗಳು) come in thirteen: ಅ ಆ ಇ ಈ ಉ ಊ ಋ ಎ ಏ ಐ ಒ ಓ ಔ ಅಂ ಅಃ. Short and long pairs — ಅ/ಆ, ಇ/ಈ, ಉ/ಊ — change meaning completely: ಕಲ (kala — learn!) versus ಕಾಲ (kaala — time/leg). Length is meaning in Kannada; stretch with care.

Consonants (ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳು) run five rows deep: ಕ ಖ ಗ ಘ ಙ, ಚ ಛ ಜ ಝ ಞ, ಟ ಠ ಡ ಢ ಣ, ತ ಥ ದ ಧ ನ, ಪ ಫ ಬ ಭ ಮ — plus ಯ ರ ಲ ವ ಶ ಷ ಸ ಹ ಳ. Round, curly, friendly — the script that looks like Telugu's twin and sounds like music.

Vowels and consonants marry into ಗುಣಿತಾಕ್ಷರಗಳು (gunitaksharas): ಕ್ + ಅ = ಕ (ka), ಕ್ + ಆ = ಕಾ (kaa). Learn the vowel-signs once and every consonant sings the same song — the system is vast but perfectly regular.

Then the crown jewels: ಳ (lla), the retroflex liquid — ಬೆಳಕು (light), ಕಳು (send); and ಣ (nna), the retroflex nasal — ಕಣ್ಣು (eye). Natives will grin when you land them; the grin is worth weeks of practice.

topics.desc: ಒಂದು ಎರಡು ಮೂರು to ನೂರು — plus clock time and market-ready counting. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: International digits for daily life — prices, phones, buses all use them. Kannada has traditional number words in full use (ಒಂದು, ಹತ್ತು, ನೂರು) but modern digits in print.
faqs.q: Kannada digits or international digits?

faqs.a: Take the number, add ಗಂಟೆ (gante — hour): ಮೂರು ಗಂಟೆ (three o'clock). Half past adds -ವರೆ: ಮೂರುವರೆ is half past three. One rule, every clock in Karnataka.
faqs.q: How do I say the time in Kannada?

faqs.a: ಎಷ್ಟು? (eshtu — how much?). Then listen for the number plus ರೂಪಾಯಿ (roopaayi — rupees). Market Kannada is the fastest teacher there is.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

topics.note: A note on ಒಂದೂವರೆ, ಎರಡೂವರೆ. Half hours glue -ವರೆ to the number: ಒಂದೂವರೆ (1:30), ಮೂರುವರೆ (3:30), ಐದೂವರೆ (5:30). Every language hides one clock trick; Kannada's is ವರೆ. Learn it and sound native instantly.
paras: One to ten: ಒಂದು (ondu), ಎರಡು (eradu), ಮೂರು (mooru), ನಾಲ್ಕು (naalku), ಐದು (aidu), ಆರು (aaru), ಏಳು (elu), ಎಂಟು (entu), ಒಂಬತ್ತು (ombattu), ಹತ್ತು (hattu). Chant them in rhythm — Kannada numbers love rhythm — and they stick in days, not weeks.

Eleven to nineteen build on ಹತ್ತು: ಹನ್ನೊಂದು (11), ಹನ್ನೆರಡು (12), ಹದಿಮೂರು (13)... then the tens march: ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು (20), ಮೂವತ್ತು (30), ನಲವತ್ತು (40), ಐವತ್ತು (50), ಅರವತ್ತು (60), ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತು (70), ಎಂಬತ್ತು (80), ತೊಂಬತ್ತು (90), ನೂರು (100). Past twenty, glue tens to units — ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂದು (21) — and count to a thousand (ಸಾವಿರ) without fear.

Money runs on numbers: the currency is the ರೂಪಾಯಿ (roopaayi — rupee), and ಎಷ್ಟು? (eshtu — how much?) is the most useful sentence in Karnataka. Listen for the number, repeat it back — ಐವತ್ತು? (fifty?) — and your first Kannada transaction completes itself.

Time reuses numbers with ಗಂಟೆ (gante — hour): ಎರಡು ಗಂಟೆ (two o'clock), ಐದು ಗಂಟೆ (five o'clock). ಈಗ ಟೈಮ್ ಎಷ್ಟು? (what time is it now?) is the question; half hours add -ವರೆ. Numbers, money, clocks: one skill, three daily victories.

topics.desc: Names, homes and small talk — your first real Kannada conversations, line by line. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ನಿಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರು ಏನು? (nimma hesaru enu — what is your name?) for respect; ನಿನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು ಏನು? (ninna hesaru enu) for friends and children. Answer with ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು... (nanna hesaru — my name is...). Names first, always.
faqs.q: How do I ask someone's name?

faqs.a: ನೀವು ಎಲ್ಲಿಂದ ಬರುತ್ತೀರಿ? (where are you from?) — then answer for yourself: ನಾನು ... ಇಂದ ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ. Origin questions are the universal second question; prepare your answer before you need it.
faqs.q: How do I say where I'm from?

faqs.a: ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಮಾತಾಡಿ (please speak slowly) and ಮತ್ತೆ ಹೇಳಿ (please say it again). Said with a smile, these two sentences make every Kannada speaker slow down and help.
faqs.q: What do I say when people speak too fast?

topics.note: A note on ನೀವು, ನೀನು and ರೀ. Kannada has two yous where English has one: ನೀವು (neevu — formal/plural) and ನೀನು (neenu — familiar) — plus ರೀ (ree), the friendly respect-particle. Start with ನೀವು for every adult; let friendship invite you to ನೀನು.
paras: Every first conversation follows the same dance: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ, ನಿಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರು ಏನು? (what is your name?), ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು... (my name is...), ನೀವು ಎಲ್ಲಿಂದ ಬರುತ್ತೀರಿ? (where are you from?). Four lines, and you have had a real conversation. Practise them in order until they flow without thinking.

Small talk runs on three questions: ನೀವು ಏನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತೀರಿ? (what do you do?), ಕನ್ನಡ ಮಾತಾಡ್ತೀರಾ? (do you speak Kannada?), ಊಟ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರಾ? (have you eaten? — asked with genuine care). Answer briefly, ask back immediately — ನೀವು? — because conversations are volleys, not speeches.

When the torrent comes — and Kannada hospitality pours words — deploy the brakes: ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಮಾತಾಡಿ (please speak slowly), ನನಗೆ ಅರ್ಥವಾಗಲಿಲ್ಲ (I didn't understand), ಮತ್ತೆ ಹೇಳಿ (please say it again). Every Kannada speaker honours these instantly; they are the learner's seatbelt.

Close warmly and promise return: ನಿಮ್ಮನ್ನು ಭೇಟಿಯಾಗಿದ್ದು ಸಂತೋಷ (pleased to meet you), ಮತ್ತೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ (we'll meet again). Leave with a ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ and the door stays open — Kannada conversations end the way they begin: with folded hands.

topics.desc: ಹೋಗು, ಬಾ, ತಿನ್ನು — the twelve verbs that run daily life, plus how they bend. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Stems are orders to friends — ಹೋಗು! (go!), ಬಾ! (come!), ತಿನ್ನು! (eat!). Polite speech adds endings: ಹೋಗಿ (please go), ಬನ್ನಿ (please come). Learn stems first, politeness second, and never order a stranger.
faqs.q: Are verb stems commands?

faqs.a: ನಾನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ (I go), ನೀನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀಯ (you go), ಅವನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತಾನೆ (he goes). Person-markers on every verb — drill one verb through all persons and the pattern owns you.
faqs.q: How do Kannada verbs change?

faqs.a: ಇಲ್ಲ (illa — no/not) negates existence — ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ uses -ಇಲ್ಲ for verbs (I don't know). Kannada negation splits by word type; learn ಇಲ್ಲ for things, ಬೇಡ (beda — don't want) for refusals.
faqs.q: How do I say no to a verb?

topics.note: A note on ಬನ್ನಿ vs ಬಾ. ಬಾ (baa) orders a friend to come; ಬನ್ನಿ (banni) welcomes a guest like royalty. Same verb, different universe — the -ಇ ending is pure respect. When in doubt, add the respect: Kannada people forgive stiff politeness instantly and casual rudeness never.
paras: Twelve verbs carry daily life: ಹೋಗು (go), ಬಾ (come), ತಿನ್ನು (eat), ಕುಡಿ (drink), ಓದು (read/study), ಬರಿ (write), ಮಾಡು (do), ಮಾತಾಡು (speak), ಕೊಡು (give), ತೆಗೆದುಕೋ (take), ಇರು (be/stay), ನೋಡು (see). Memorise these stems and you can order food, find toilets, make friends and survive beautifully.

Stems bend by person in the present: ನಾನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ (I go), ನೀನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀಯ (you familiar go), ನೀವು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀರಿ (you formal go), ಅವನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತಾನೆ (he goes). The -ಉತ್ತ- (utta) infix marks present tense across nearly every verb — one infix, hundreds of verbs, instant sentences.

Polite commands add -ಇ: ಹೋಗಿ (please go), ಬನ್ನಿ (please come), ತಿನ್ನಿ (please eat), ಹೇಳಿ (please say). This one ending turns every order into an invitation — it is the most useful suffix in Kannada, worth more than a hundred nouns.

Negation and existence close the kit: ಇದೆ (ide — it is / there is) anchors locations — ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಮೇಜಿನ ಮೇಲೆ ಇದೆ (the book is on the table). ಇಲ್ಲ (illa — there isn't) removes — ಹಣ ಇಲ್ಲ (no money). Twelve verbs plus ಇದೆ/ಇಲ್ಲ: the engine room of Kannada.

faqs.a: Time words first: ಇಂದು (today), ನಾಳೆ (tomorrow), ನಿನ್ನೆ (yesterday), ಈಗ (now). You will use them ten times a day — shopping, planning, chatting — while rare nouns gather dust.
faqs.q: Which words pay off fastest?

faqs.a: Kannada happily absorbs English — ಬಸ್ (bus), ಟಿಕೆಟ್ (ticket), ಆಫೀಸು (office). Use the pure Kannada word when you know it, the loanword when you don't. Fluency first, purity later.
faqs.q: Is mixing English okay?

faqs.a: Nouns first, verbs second, adjectives third. With fifty nouns and the twelve verbs from the verbs page, you can point, ask and survive — grammar glues them later.
faqs.q: Nouns or verbs first?

topics.note: A note on ಇಂದು, ನಾಳೆ, ನಿನ್ನೆ. Kannada time words pivot around today: ಇಂದು (indu — today), ನಾಳೆ (naale — tomorrow), ನಿನ್ನೆ (ninne — yesterday). Master this trio and half your daily sentences assemble themselves — ನಾಳೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ (see you tomorrow) alone is worth the lesson.
paras: Survival runs on nouns: ನೀರು (neeru — water), ಆಹಾರ (aahaara — food), ಮನೆ (mane — home), ಹಣ (hana — money), ಸಮಯ (samaya — time). Five words, and you can ask for water, find home, handle money and ask the time — the entire first day in a new city.

Movement words come next: ರಸ್ತೆ (raste — road), ಬಸ್ (bas — bus), ಅಂಗಡಿ (angadi — shop), ಶಾಲೆ (shaale — school). Karnataka moves by bus and foot; knowing ಬಸ್ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (where is the bus stand?) saves more time than any app.

Opinions need adjectives: ಒಳ್ಳೆ (olle — good), ದೊಡ್ಡ (dodda — big), ಚಿಕ್ಕ (chikka — small), ಹೊಸ (hosa — new), ಹಳೆಯ (haleya — old). ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು (olleyadu — that's good) approves everything from food to plans — the most useful single opinion in Kannada.

Weather and mood close the kit: ಮಳೆ (male — rain) matters half the year, ಬಿಸಿಲು (bisilu — sun/heat) the other half. ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತಿದೆ (rain is coming) starts conversations with strangers; in Karnataka, weather talk is friendship's front door.

topics.desc: Dose, idli, bisibelebaat — order like a local, from breakfast to bill. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Point and say ಇದು ಒಂದು (idu ondu — one of these) — it works in every darshini, canteen and bakery in Karnataka. Add ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು (please) and a smile; grammar can wait until dessert.
faqs.q: How do I order with almost no Kannada?

faqs.a: ಖಾರ ಕಮ್ಮಿ (khaara kammi — less spicy, please). Kannada food honours chilli deeply; this one sentence saves sensitive stomachs while keeping every flavour.
faqs.q: How do I ask for less spicy food?

faqs.a: ರುಚಿಯಾಗಿದೆ (ruchiyaagide — it's delicious). Say it to the cook, the server, the ajji who packed your lunch — it is the highest compliment in Kannada food culture.
faqs.q: How do I praise the food?

topics.note: A note on ಬಿಸಿಬೇಳೆಬಾತ್. Bisibelebaat — hot lentil-rice, vegetables, ghee melting on top — is Karnataka on a plate. Order it at any darshini, mix with potato chips and boondi, and understand the state in one meal.
paras: Breakfast is the glory: ದೋಸೆ (dose — crisp crepe), ಇಡ್ಲಿ (idli — steamed cakes), ಪೂರಿ (poori — puffed bread), ವಡೆ (vade — savoury doughnut), all served with ಸಾಂಬಾರು (saambaaru) and ಚಟ್ನಿ (chutney). ಟಿಫಿನ್ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರಾ? (have you had tiffin?) is asked with love — answer honestly, then accept seconds.

Meals centre on ಊಟ (oota — the rice meal): ಅನ್ನ (anna — rice), ಸಾಂಬಾರು, ಸಾರು (saaru — pepper-tamarind soup), ಮೊಸರು (mosaru — curd), ಹಪ್ಪಳ (happala — crisp papad). Served on banana leaves at weddings, eaten with the right hand — ಊಟ ರೆಡೀನಾ? (is the meal ready?) is the happiest question.

Taste words steer every order: ಖಾರ (khaara — spicy), ಸಿಹಿ (sihi — sweet), ಹುಳಿ (huli — sour), ಉಪ್ಪು (uppu — salt). ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಉಪ್ಪು (a little salt), ಸಕ್ಕರೆ ಬೇಡ (no sugar) — with taste words, your plate obeys you.

Drinks and bills close the meal: ಕಾಫಿ (filter coffee), ಟೀ (tea), ಮಜ್ಜಿಗೆ (majjige — buttermilk), ಹಣ್ಣಿನ ರಸ (hannina rasa — juice). ಬಿಲ್ ಕೊಡಿ (please give the bill) ends it; ರುಚಿಯಾಗಿತ್ತು (it was delicious) guarantees a smile on your way out.

faqs.a: ಶ (palatal, tongue high — ಶಾಲೆ), ಷ (retroflex, curled — ಕಷ್ಟ), ಸ (dental, on teeth — ಸಮಯ). Three s-sounds where English has one; Kannada ears hear all three instantly.
faqs.q: Why three different s sounds?

faqs.a: ಳ is retroflex — tongue curled back: ಬೆಳಕು (light), ಕಳುಹಿಸು (send). ಲ is dental — tongue on teeth. Say la-la sliding tongue back and feel the shift.
faqs.q: How do I make the ಳ sound?

faqs.a: Ottaksharas: ಕ್ಷ (ksha — ಕ್ಷಮೆ), ಜ್ಞ (jna — ಜ್ಞಾನ), ತ್ರ (tra). Pronounce each part quickly in sequence — k+sha, j+na. Ottaksharas look fierce and behave kindly.
faqs.q: What are those stacked letters?

topics.note: A note on ಳ (lla). Kannada's liquid signature: curl the tongue back WITHOUT touching the roof, and voice it — ಬೆಳಕು (light), ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ (silver), ಕಳೆ (weed). Children take years to perfect it, so forgive yourself months — then enjoy the applause.
paras: The three sibilants sort by tongue: ಶ (palatal — ಶಾಲೆ, school), ಷ (retroflex — ಕಷ್ಟ, difficulty), ಸ (dental — ಸಮಯ, time). Say sha-sha-sa sliding the tongue from high to curled to teeth — three letters, one glide.
The liquid ಳ curls back: ಬೆಳಕು (belaku — light), ಕಳುಹಿಸು (kaluhisu — send). Contrast ಲ (dental, tongue on teeth) with ಳ (retroflex, curled). Glide la-lla daily; the roof-touch becomes reflex.

Dental versus retroflex stops: ತ (teeth — ತಾಯಿ, mother) against ಟ (roof — ಕೋಟೆ, fort). Hold a finger to your lips: dentals puff forward, retroflexes pop upward. Ten minutes of ತ-ಟ alternation retunes the mouth within a week.

The rest behave kindly: ಚ is cha at word start (ಚಂದ) softening inside words, ರ rolls lightly (ಮರ), and long vowels simply hold double — ಆ, ಈ, ಊ. Kannada spelling mirrors speech faithfully: pronounce what you see, and you are right nine times in ten.

topics.desc: Verb last, respect built in — Kannada grammar in plain English, no jargon walls. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Put the verb last: ನಾನು ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಓದುತ್ತೇನೆ (I book read). Subject-Object-Verb, always. English instincts will fight you for a week; then SOV feels like home.
faqs.q: Where does the verb go?

faqs.a: ನನಗೆ (nanage — to me), ನಿನಗೆ (ninage — to you familiar), ನಿಮಗೆ (nimage — to you formal). ನನಗೆ ನೀರು ಬೇಕು (I want water) is literally to-me water is-wanted — Kannada wants flow toward people.
faqs.q: How do I say I want something?

faqs.a: ಇದು (idu — this, near me), ಅದು (adu — that, far). ಇದು ಏನು? (what is this?) points at anything within reach; mastery takes one shopping trip.
faqs.q: How do this and that work?

topics.note: A note on -ಗೆ (ge). Kannada's dative ending aims verbs at people and places: ನನಗೆ (to me), ಶಾಲೆಗೆ (to school), ಮನೆಗೆ (homeward). Sentences like ನನಗೆ ಅರ್ಥವಾಯಿತು (to-me it-is-understood = I understand) reveal Kannada's worldview: experiences come TO you.
paras: Kannada sentences end with the verb: ನಾನು ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಓದುತ್ತೇನೆ (I — book — read). Subject first, object middle, verb last — SOV, the order of half the world's languages. Rearrange your English instincts once, and every Kannada sentence parses cleanly.

Small endings do heavy work: -ಅಲ್ಲಿ (alli — in/on) places things — ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ (at home), ಮೇಜಿನ ಮೇಲೆ (on the table); -ಜೊತೆ (jote — with) joins company — ಸ್ನೇಹಿತನ ಜೊತೆ (with a friend); -ಗೆ (ge) aims motion and wanting — ಶಾಲೆಗೆ (to school), ನನಗೆ ಬೇಕು (I want). Endings, not word order, carry Kannada meaning.

Questions rise at the end: ನೀವು ಎಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀರಿ? (where are you going?) — ಎಲ್ಲಿ (where), ಏನು (what), ಯಾರು (who), ಏಕೆ (why), ಹೇಗೆ (how), ಯಾವಾಗ (when). Yes-no questions add -ಆ (-aa): ಊಟ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರಾ? (have you eaten?). Question words plus rising tone — asking is easy.

Negation splits three ways: ಇಲ್ಲ (illa) denies existence — ಹಣ ಇಲ್ಲ (no money); verb endings deny actions — ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (I don't know); ಬೇಡ (beda) refuses — ಸಕ್ಕರೆ ಬೇಡ (no sugar, thanks). Three no's for three jobs — Kannada refuses precisely.

faqs.a: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ, ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ, ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು — five words, infinite mileage. Add ನಾನು and ನೀವು and you can introduce yourself to anyone in Karnataka.
faqs.q: What are the first five words?

faqs.a: Fifteen focused minutes beat two distracted hours. One topic page, every speaker tapped, five words reviewed — daily beats heroic.
faqs.q: How much should I study daily?

faqs.a: No — speak first, script second. Roman letters carry you through months of conversation; the alphabet page waits patiently until curiosity pulls you in.

topics.note: A note on ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ and ಹೂಂ. Kannada yes comes in three flavours: ಹೌದು (haudu — respectful yes), ಸರಿ (sari — okay/agreed), ಹೂಂ (hoom — casual yeah). Learners live on ಹೌದು and ಸರಿ — respectful, warm, never wrong. Save ಹೂಂ for friends.
paras: Week one needs eleven words: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ (hello), ಹೌದು (yes), ಸರಿ (okay), ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (thanks), ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು (please), ನಾನು (I), ನೀವು (you, formal), ಇದು ಏನು? (what is this?), ಅರ್ಥವಾಯಿತು (I understand), ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (I don't know), ಹೋಗೋಣ (let's go). Eleven words, and you can greet, agree, thank, ask, confess ignorance and move — the whole beginner game.
Pronouns branch early: ನಾನು (I), ನೀವು (you formal/plural), ನೀನು (you familiar), ಅವನು/ಅವಳು (he/she), ಅವರು (they formal), ನಾವು (we). ನಾವು ಹೋಗೋಣ (let's go, all of us) is Kannada's warmest invitation.

Quantity words multiply everything: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ (a little), ತುಂಬಾ (a lot), ಸಾಕು (enough), ಮಾತ್ರ (only). ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕನ್ನಡ ಮಾತಾಡ್ತೀನಿ (I speak a little Kannada) is the perfect learner's confession — humble, charming, instantly rewarded with help.

Action invitations close week one: ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಬನ್ನಿ (come here), ಕೂತ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ (please sit), ತಿನ್ನಿ (please eat), ಹೋಗೋಣ (let's go). These four run hospitality, the beating heart of Kannada culture — learn them and you stop being a guest and start being family.

topics.desc: ಅಮ್ಮ, ಅಪ್ಪ, ಅಣ್ಣ, ಅಕ್ಕ — family words, including the elder-younger split. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Yes — Kannada splits siblings by age: ಅಣ್ಣ (elder brother) versus ತಮ್ಮ (younger brother), ಅಕ್ಕ (elder sister) versus ತಂಗಿ (younger sister). Age order is grammar in Kannada families.
faqs.q: Why two words for brother?

faqs.a: ಅಣ್ಣ (anna) and ಅಕ್ಕ (akka) address any slightly-older man or woman — shopkeepers, colleagues, strangers. It borrows family warmth for the whole world.
faqs.q: Can I call strangers anna and akka?

faqs.a: ನಿಮ್ಮ ಕುಟುಂಬದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಷ್ಟು ಜನ? (how many people in your family?) — then listen proudly to the answer. Family questions are love in Kannada culture.
faqs.q: How do I ask about family?

topics.lede: ಅಮ್ಮ, ಅಪ್ಪ, ಅಣ್ಣ, ಅಕ್ಕ — family, including the elder-younger split.
topics.note: A note on ಅಜ್ಜ, ಅಜ್ಜಿ. Kannada grandparents share short sweet names: ಅಜ್ಜ (ajja — grandfather) and ಅಜ್ಜಿ (ajji — grandmother) — no side-splitting needed. Learners need the big six first; the full map unfolds at weddings.
paras: Parents anchor everything: ಅಮ್ಮ (amma — mother) and ಅಪ್ಪ (appa — father) — the first words of every Kannada child and the warmest words in the language. ಅಮ್ಮ calls across market crowds; ಅಪ್ಪ advises over evening coffee. Learn them with love, not just memory.

Siblings split by age, never blend: ಅಣ್ಣ (elder brother), ತಮ್ಮ (younger brother), ಅಕ್ಕ (elder sister), ತಂಗಿ (younger sister). There is no plain brother — every brother is elder or younger, and the word you choose declares the hierarchy. Ask ages early; address correctly always.

Grandparents rule the roost: ಅಜ್ಜ (ajja — grandfather) and ಅಜ್ಜಿ (ajji — grandmother) — storytellers, sweet-sneakers, family courts of final appeal. ಅಜ್ಜಿ ಕತೆ (grandmother's tale) is a whole genre; ಅಜ್ಜ advice ends arguments. Respect flows upward; treats flow down.

The wider net holds daily life: ಮಾವ (uncle), ಅತ್ತೆ (auntie), ಗಂಡ (husband), ಹೆಂಡತಿ (wife), ಕುಟುಂಬ (family itself). ನನ್ನ ಕುಟುಂಬ (my family) introduces them all — practise the sentence with your own names filled in, because you will say it at every Kannada gathering forever.
topics.title: Family words

topics.desc: Seven days, four day-parts, weeks and months — Kannada time from morning to month. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Start the week Sunday like Kannada calendars: ಭಾನುವಾರ, ಸೋಮವಾರ, ಮಂಗಳವಾರ, ಬುಧವಾರ, ಗುರುವಾರ, ಶುಕ್ರವಾರ, ಶನಿವಾರ. Chant them in order — rhythm makes them permanent.
faqs.q: How do I memorise the days?

faqs.a: ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ (morning), ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ (afternoon), ಸಂಜೆ (evening), ರಾತ್ರಿ (night). Greetings, meals and plans all key off these four — ಶುಭಸಂಜೆ (good evening) after four-ish.
faqs.q: How does Kannada split the day?

faqs.a: ವಾರ (vaara — week), ತಿಂಗಳು (tingalu — month), ವರ್ಷ (varsha — year). ಮುಂದಿನ ವಾರ (next week), ಈ ತಿಂಗಳು (this month) — plans assemble instantly.
faqs.q: Week, month, year?

topics.lede: Seven days, four day-parts, weeks and months — Kannada time fully told.

topics.note: A note on ಶುಕ್ರವಾರ and ಮಂಗಳವಾರ. Friday (ಶುಕ್ರವಾರ) and Tuesday (ಮಂಗಳವಾರ) are auspicious days — temples fill, new ventures launch, ದೇವಿ worship peaks. Knowing the days means knowing the rhythm: never schedule a sceptical meeting on a festival Friday.
paras: The week runs Sunday-first: ಭಾನುವಾರ (Sunday), ಸೋಮವಾರ (Monday), ಮಂಗಳವಾರ (Tuesday), ಬುಧವಾರ (Wednesday), ಗುರುವಾರ (Thursday), ಶುಕ್ರವಾರ (Friday), ಶನಿವಾರ (Saturday). Planet-named like most of Asia — the sky keeps Kannada's calendar, and every day ends in ವಾರ.

Day-parts steer greetings and meals: ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ (morning — ಶುಭೋದಯ), ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ (afternoon — lunch/oota o'clock), ಸಂಜೆ (evening — ಶುಭಸಂಜೆ, coffee round two), ರಾತ್ರಿ (night — goodnight is usually just ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ with a smile).

Bigger units plan life: ವಾರ (week), ತಿಂಗಳು (month), ವರ್ಷ (year) — ಮುಂದಿನ ವಾರ (next week), ಕಳೆದ ತಿಂಗಳು (last month), ಈ ವರ್ಷ (this year). Kannada plans in weeks for errands, months for visits, years for weddings.

Dates assemble simply: ದಿನಾಂಕ (dinaanka — date), ಮೊದಲನೇ ತಾರೀಕು (first), ಇಂದು ದಿನಾಂಕ ಎಷ್ಟು? (what's today's date?). Numbers from the numbers page slot straight in — ಹದಿನೈದನೇ ತಾರೀಕು (the 15th). Time, dates, plans: one page, total coverage.

topics.desc: Stations, directions, tickets and toilets — travel Kannada that gets you there. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ...ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (...elli — where is...?) plus a pointing finger. ಬಸ್ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? ರೈಲ್ವೆ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? One pattern, every destination in Karnataka.
faqs.q: How do I ask where things are?

faqs.a: ಎಡ (left), ಬಲ (right), ನೇರವಾಗಿ (straight) — then ಹತ್ತಿರ (near) and ದೂರ (far). Kannada directions come with generous hand-waving; watch the hands as well as the words.
faqs.q: Left, right, straight?

faqs.a: ಶೌಚಾಲಯ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (where is the toilet?) — say it clearly, without embarrassment. Every bus stand, station and restaurant understands instantly.
faqs.q: How do I find a toilet?

topics.note: A note on ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ. ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ (nildaana — station/stand) anchors every journey: ಬಸ್ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ (bus stand), ರೈಲ್ವೆ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ (railway station), ವಿಮಾನ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ (airport). Learn the pattern once — vehicle + ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ — and every signboard in Karnataka reads itself.
paras: Destinations unlock with one ending: ಬಸ್ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ (bus stand), ರೈಲ್ವೆ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ (railway station), ವಿಮಾನ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ (airport), ಹೋಟೆಲ್ (hotel). Add ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (where?) and you can find every transport hub in the state — ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? is the traveller's master key.

Directions come in threes: ಎಡ (left), ಬಲ (right), ನೇರವಾಗಿ (straight ahead) — plus ಹತ್ತಿರ (nearby) and ದೂರ (far). ಎಡಗಡೆ (on the left side), ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಹೋಗಿ (go straight) — follow the words, watch the inevitable hand gestures, arrive smiling.

Tickets and seats run the journey: ಟಿಕೆಟ್ (ticket), ಒಂದು ಟಿಕೆಟ್ (one ticket), ಎಷ್ಟು? (how much?), ಸೀಟು (seatu — seat). ಬಸ್ ಯಾವಾಗ ಬರುತ್ತೆ? (when does the bus come?) — asked at every stand, answered with cheerful vagueness. Patience is also vocabulary.

Emergencies and essentials close the kit: ಸಹಾಯ (help), ಶೌಚಾಲಯ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (where is the toilet?), ನೀರು (water), ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ (hospital). Hope never to need ನನಗೆ ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡಿ (please help) — but carry it always, like travel insurance in a single word.

topics.desc: Prices, bargaining and colours — shop in Kannada from first price to final deal. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ಬೆಲೆ ಎಷ್ಟು? (what's the price?) — then ಎಷ್ಟು? (how much?) for everything else. Two questions, every shop in Karnataka.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

faqs.a: ತುಂಬಾ ದುಬಾರಿ (too costly) with a smile, then ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ (reduce a little, please). Bargaining is friendly theatre — play your part warmly and the price moves.
faqs.q: How do I bargain politely?

faqs.a: Start with five: ಕೆಂಪು (red), ನೀಲಿ (blue), ಹಸಿರು (green), ಹಳದಿ (yellow), ಬಿಳಿ (white). ಬೇರೆ ಬಣ್ಣ (different colour) shows them all.
faqs.q: Which colours first?

topics.note: A note on ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ. ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ (swalpa kadime maadi — please reduce a little) is the magic sentence of Karnataka markets. Said smiling, it opens every negotiation; said with ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತೇನೆ (I'll take it) right after, it closes most. Bargaining respects the dance — never the demand.
paras: Prices open every transaction: ಬೆಲೆ ಎಷ್ಟು? (what's the price?), ಎಷ್ಟು? (how much?), ಇದು ಬೆಲೆ ಎಷ್ಟು? (what's this one's price?). Listen for the number plus ರೂಪಾಯಿ — repeat it back to confirm — ಐವತ್ತು? (fifty?) — and you are already shopping in Kannada.

Bargaining follows the friendly script: ತುಂಬಾ ದುಬಾರಿ (too costly), ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ (reduce a little), ಡಿಸ್ಕೌಂಟ್ ಇದೆಯಾ? (any discount?). Start walking away slowly — ಧನ್ಯವಾದ, ನೋಡ್ತೀನಿ (thanks, I'll look around) — and the real price often chases you down the street.

Sizes and colours refine the hunt: ದೊಡ್ಡದು (the bigger one), ಚಿಕ್ಕದು (the smaller one), ಹೊಸದು (a new one), ಬೇರೆ ಬಣ್ಣ (a different colour). Point, name the change, nod — Kannada shopkeepers read gestures fluently and reward attempts instantly.

Colours close the sale: ಕೆಂಪು (red), ನೀಲಿ (blue), ಹಸಿರು (green), ಹಳದಿ (yellow), ಬಿಳಿ (white), ಕಪ್ಪು (black). ಕೆಂಪು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದೆ (the red looks good) — then ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತೇನೆ (I'll take it). Deal done, in Kannada, with a smile on both sides.

topics.desc: Help, doctor, hospital — emergency Kannada you hope to never need. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ನನಗೆ ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡಿ (please help me) — loud, clear, repeated. Add ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (where is the hospital?) and Kannada crowds mobilise instantly.
faqs.q: What is the one emergency sentence?

faqs.a: Point and say ಇಲ್ಲಿ ನೋವಾಗಿದೆ (it hurts here). Then ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸರಿಯಿಲ್ಲ (I feel unwell) and ಡಾಕ್ಟರ್ ಬೇಕು (I need a doctor). Pain plus pointing crosses every language gap.
faqs.q: How do I explain pain?

faqs.a: ಕಳೆದುಹೋಗಿದೆ (it is lost) — ಹಣ ಕಳೆದುಹೋಗಿದೆ (money lost), ಬ್ಯಾಗ್ ಕಳೆದುಹೋಗಿದೆ (bag lost). Then ಪೋಲೀಸ್ ಸ್ಟೇಷನ್ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (where is the police station?).
faqs.q: How do I report something lost?

topics.lede: Help, doctor, hospital — emergency Kannada you hope to never need.
topics.note: A note on ಸಹಾಯ. ಸಹಾಯ (sahaaya — help) is Kannada's shortest lifeline — shout it and crowds come running. Karnataka's bystander culture is famously kind: strangers will escort you to hospitals, translate for doctors, and refuse thanks. Ask loudly; receive gratefully.
paras: The core three save lives: ಸಹಾಯ (help), ಅಪಾಯ (danger), ತುರ್ತು (emergency). ನನಗೆ ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡಿ (please help me) — say it to anyone, anywhere. Kannada crowds respond to distress calls faster than any app; your job is only to ask.

Medical words route the rescue: ಡಾಕ್ಟರ್ (doctor), ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ (hospital), ಔಷಧಿ (medicine), ಮೆಡಿಕಲ್ ಶಾಪ್ (pharmacy). ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (where is the hospital?) plus a taxi wave — in cities, help arrives in minutes.

Symptoms speak simply: ಇಲ್ಲಿ ನೋವಾಗಿದೆ (it hurts here — point!), ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಸರಿಯಿಲ್ಲ (I feel unwell), ತಲೆನೋವು (headache), ಜ್ವರ (fever). Pain words plus pointing hands diagnose across every language barrier on earth.

Danger and loss close the kit: ಬೆಂಕಿ (fire), ಕಳ್ಳ (thief), ಪೋಲೀಸರು (police), ಕಳೆದುಹೋಗಿದೆ (it's lost), ಎಂಬಸಿ (embassy). Memorise these cold — emergencies never wait for phrasebooks, and ten minutes of drilling buys total peace of mind.
topics.title: Emergency Kannada

topics.desc: ನೀವು or ನೀನು? ಬನ್ನಿ or ಬಾ? Respect levels, decoded with examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ನೀವು for every adult you don't know well — shopkeepers, officials, elders, strangers. ನೀನು waits for close friends, children and family. Wrong-side errors embarrass; learners are forgiven, but respect first is always safest.
faqs.q: When do I use ನೀವು?

faqs.a: Add -ಇ: ಬಾ becomes ಬನ್ನಿ, ಮಾಡು becomes ಮಾಡಿ, ಹೇಳು becomes ಹೇಳಿ. One ending, instant politeness — the highest-value suffix in Kannada.
faqs.q: How do I make a command polite?

faqs.a: ರೀ (ree — respectful hey) and ಅಮ್ಮ (amma — madam) — or ಸಾರ್ (saar) borrowed and beloved. ರೀ, ಟೈಮ್ ಎಷ್ಟು? (excuse me, what time is it?). Better than pointing and shouting in any language.
faqs.q: How do I address strangers?

topics.lede: ನೀವು or ನೀನು? ಬನ್ನಿ or ಬಾ? Respect levels, decoded.
topics.note: A note on ರೀ. ರೀ (ree) is Kannada's pocket-sized respect — attach it anywhere and warmth ignites: ಬನ್ನಿ ರೀ (do come), ನೋಡಿ ರೀ (please see), ಹೇಳಿ ರೀ (please tell). Two sounds that upgrade every request instantly.
paras: Kannada has two yous: ನೀವು (formal/plural — strangers, elders, officials) and ನೀನು (familiar — friends, children, family). English erased this distinction centuries ago; Kannada keeps it razor-sharp. Every conversation opens with an invisible choice — make it consciously, and make it respectful.

Verbs mirror the split: ಬನ್ನಿ (please come) versus ಬಾ (come!), ಹೇಳಿ (please say) versus ಹೇಳು (say!), ಹೋಗಿ (please go) versus ಹೋಗು (go!). The -ಇ ending is pure respect — same verb, different universe. Stem-alone orders bark; -ಇ invites.

Giving and forgiving show the range: ಕೊಡಿ (please give) versus ಕೊಡು (give!), ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ (please forgive) versus ಕ್ಷಮಿಸು (forgive, familiar). Beggars and kings both hear ಕೊಡಿ — politeness in Kannada costs nothing and buys everything.

Strangers get particles and titles: ರೀ (respectful hey), ಅಮ್ಮ (madam), ಅಣ್ಣ (brother), ಅಕ್ಕ (sister). ರೀ, ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡಿ (excuse me, please help) opens any door; barking orders at strangers closes them. Kannada warmth is earned with two syllables of respect.
topics.title: Formal and informal Kannada

topics.desc: Verb-first sentences, ನಾನು ಬೇಕು, ಇಲ್ಲ vs ಅಲ್ಲ — fix the classic errors. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: English order with Kannada words: ನಾನು ಹೋಗು instead of ನಾನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ, verb first, question words misplaced. Cure: every sentence ends with the verb — practise SOV until English order feels foreign.
faqs.q: What is the most common mistake?

faqs.a: Wanting flows toward people: ನನಗೆ ಬೇಕು (to-me it-is-wanted), never ನಾನು ಬೇಕು. One of Kannada's deepest patterns — experiences come TO you — and beginners fight it for weeks.
faqs.q: Why is ನಾನು ಬೇಕು wrong?

faqs.a: ಇಲ್ಲ denies existence and possession — ಹಣ ಇಲ್ಲ (no money); ಅಲ್ಲ denies identity — ನಾನು ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿ ಅಲ್ಲ (I am not a student). Two no's, two jobs, zero overlap.
faqs.q: ಇಲ್ಲ or ಅಲ್ಲ?

topics.lede: Verb-first sentences, ನಾನು ಬೇಕು, ಇಲ್ಲ vs ಅಲ್ಲ — fix them all.
topics.note: A note on ತಪ್ಪು. ತಪ್ಪು (tappu — mistake) is the kindest word in this lesson — ನನ್ನ ತಪ್ಪು (my mistake) disarms every situation. Kannada people adore learners who err boldly and laugh warmly; the only true ತಪ್ಪು is silence.
paras: Mistake one: English word order. ನಾನು ಹೋಗು (I go — bare stem, wrong) instead of ನಾನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ (I go — conjugated, right); verbs wandering mid-sentence instead of anchoring the end. Kannada is verb-final, always — SOV is not a suggestion, it is the law.

Mistake two: ನಾನು ಬೇಕು (I want — wrong) instead of ನನಗೆ ಬೇಕು (to-me wanted — right). Kannada wanting flows toward the wanter; English wanting fires from the wanter. Flip the arrow and dozens of sentences — ನನಗೆ ಅರ್ಥವಾಯಿತು, ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು — unlock at once.

Mistake three: one-size no. ಇಲ್ಲ denies existence — ಹಣ ಇಲ್ಲ (there's no money); ಅಲ್ಲ denies identity — ನಾನು ಟೀಚರ್ ಅಲ್ಲ (I am not a teacher). Beginners spray ಇಲ್ಲ everywhere; natives smile and correct. Learn both no's, use each precisely.

Mistake four: rushing sounds — flat long vowels, merged sibilants, skipped -ಇ. ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ (slowly), ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ (correctly), ಮತ್ತೆ (again): the holy trinity of repair. ಪ್ರಯತ್ನ (effort) plus ಅಭ್ಯಾಸ (practice) plus ತಾಳ್ಮೆ (patience) — and ಅಭಿನಂದನೆಗಳು, mistakes become fluency.
topics.title: Mistakes every learner makes

topics.desc: Stop translating in your head — shadowing, thinking aloud and brave first speeches. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Shadow natives: play a Kannada sentence, repeat it aloud half a second behind, matching rhythm and melody. Ten minutes daily rewires your mouth faster than any textbook.
faqs.q: What is the fastest speaking drill?

faqs.a: Yes — narrate your day in Kannada: ನಾನು ಕಾಫಿ ಕುಡಿಯುತ್ತಿದ್ದೇನೆ (I'm drinking coffee), ನಾನು ಶಾಲೆಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ. Thinking aloud turns dead time into speaking practice.
faqs.q: Should I talk to myself in Kannada?

faqs.a: Perfectionism. Kannada people reward every attempt and correct with love — ಮಾತಾಡಿ, ತಪ್ಪು ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ (speak, mistakes are fine). Fluency is corrected mistakes, stacked daily.
faqs.q: What blocks speaking most?

topics.note: A note on ಮಾತಾಡೋಣ. ಮಾತಾಡೋಣ (maataadona — let's speak / we may speak) is permission and invitation in one word — ಬನ್ನಿ, ಕನ್ನಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತಾಡೋಣ (come, let's speak in Kannada). Say it to every patient listener; doors, hearts and vocabularies open together.
paras: Speaking starts with shadowing: play a Kannada line, echo it half a beat behind, copying music more than words. ಸಂಭಾಷಣೆ (conversation) is rhythm before grammar — shadow ten minutes daily and your mouth learns Kannada's dance while your brain watches.

Questions and answers volley practice: ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ (question) out, ಉತ್ತರ (answer) back. Ask yourself everything — ಇದು ಏನು? ಎಲ್ಲಿ? ಏಕೆ? — and answer aloud. Self-volleys feel silly for a day, then feel like fluency arriving.

Opinions and stories stretch speeches: ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯ (opinion), ಸತ್ಯ (truth), ಕತೆ (story). ನನ್ನ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯ... (in my opinion...) forces full sentences; ಕತೆ ಹೇಳಿ (tell a story) forces sequences. Opinions build sentences; stories build speakers.

Courage closes the circuit: ಧೈರ್ಯ (courage) speaks first and perfects later. ಹಾಡು (songs) loosen tongues, ನಗು (laughter) dissolves fear, ಮೌನ (pauses) are allowed. Speak badly today — ಭಾಷಣ (speech) improves only in motion.
topics.title: Speaking practice

topics.desc: Fast speech, films and radio — train your ears until Kannada sounds slow. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Spoken Kannada contracts: ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ melts toward ಹೋಗ್ತೀನಿ, ಮಾಡುತ್ತೇನೆ toward ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ. Learn the full forms first, then meet the street forms — this page bridges both.
faqs.q: Why is spoken Kannada so fast?

faqs.a: Children's films and songs first — clear speech, simple stories, endless repetition. Then ರೇಡಿಯೋ dramas, then full ಸಿನಿಮಾ (cinema). Difficulty ladders beat difficulty cliffs.
faqs.q: What should I listen to first?

faqs.a: Catch the question words — ಏನು, ಎಲ್ಲಿ, ಯಾರು, ಯಾವಾಗ — and the verb at the end. Questions plus verbs carry eighty percent of meaning; the rest is decoration.
faqs.q: How do I catch meaning in fast speech?

topics.note: A note on ಅರ್ಥವಾಯಿತಾ? ಅರ್ಥವಾಯಿತಾ? (arthavaayitaa — do you understand?) is the kindest question in Kannada — teachers, friends and auto drivers ask it constantly. Answer ಅರ್ಥವಾಯಿತು (understood) or ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ (little by little); honesty tunes every speaker to your level.
paras: Listening begins with attention: ಗಮನ (attention) — ಗಮನವಿಟ್ಟು ಕೇಳಿ (listen carefully). Kannada sentences save the verb for last, so ears must hold the whole sentence before meaning lands. Patience is a listening skill; practise holding, not guessing.

Street Kannada contracts beautifully: ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ → ಹೋಗ್ತೀನಿ, ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ → ಬರ್ತೀನಿ. Textbooks teach the full forms; ears must learn the melted ones. Listen for the verb-ghost at sentence end — the meaning hides there.

Media ladders the difficulty: ಹಾಡು (songs) first — slow, repetitive, emotional; ಸುದ್ದಿ (news) next — clear, formal, standard; ರೇಡಿಯೋ (radio) drama third — fast, natural, fun; ಸಿನಿಮಾ (films) last — slang, speed, glory. Climb rung by rung; never leap.

Active listening closes the loop: ಮತ್ತೆ ಕೇಳಿ (listen again), ಧ್ವನಿ (sound) by ಧ್ವನಿ. Replay each line three times — once for music, once for words, once for meaning. Three passes per line, ten lines per day: ears transform within a month.

topics.desc: Words to sentences to stories — reading Kannada from first signs to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Signboards: ಅಂಗಡಿ (shop), ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ (station), ಹೋಟೆಲ್ (restaurant) — big letters, daily repetition, instant rewards. Streets teach faster than textbooks.
faqs.q: What should I read first?

faqs.a: Children's books — short ವಾಕ್ಯ (sentences), pictures for context, full ottaksharas. Then comics, then ದಿನಪತ್ರಿಕೆ headlines, then articles.
faqs.q: When am I ready for books?

faqs.a: Keep a ನಿಘಂಟು (dictionary) app open and mine unknown words — five per page, no more. Reading with a dictionary beats studying word lists: context glues memory.
faqs.q: How do I handle unknown words?

topics.lede: Words to sentences to stories — reading from first signs to full pages.
topics.note: A note on ದಿನಪತ್ರಿಕೆ. Kannada newspapers — ಪ್ರಜಾವಾಣಿ, ವಿಜಯವಾಣಿ — use formal written Kannada, nobler than street speech. Headlines first: big type, short lines, daily habit. One headline a day keeps illiteracy away.
paras: Reading starts with words: ಪದ (word) by ಪದ — ಓದಿ (please read) signs, labels, names. Kannada spelling mirrors speech, so sounding out works: see ಅಂಗಡಿ, say angadi, know shop. Phonetic scripts reward beginners richly.

Sentences assemble next: ವಾಕ್ಯ (sentence) — subject, object, verb-last. Read SOV sentences end-first for meaning: find the verb, then ask who-did-what. Backwards parsing feels odd for a week, then automatic forever.

Paragraphs and articles follow: ಪ್ಯಾರಾ (paragraph), ಪ್ರಬಂಧ (article), ಕವಿತೆ (poem). Children's stories first — short, illustrated, kind — then ಪತ್ರಿಕೆ (magazines), then ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ (literature) itself. Kannada's written heritage spans fifteen centuries; start at the shallow end.

Dictionaries deepen everything: ನಿಘಂಟು (dictionary) — five new words per page, written down, reviewed nightly. Reading without recording entertains; reading with recording teaches. Mine every page; keep every gem.
topics.title: Reading Kannada

topics.desc: Letters to lists to letters — writing Kannada from first strokes to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Round strokes before all: Kannada letters flow circular — ಅ, ಆ, ಉ, ಎ — so practise circles and hooks first. Trace big, shrink slowly; ಕೈಬರಹ (handwriting) beautifies with mileage.
faqs.q: How do I start writing Kannada?

faqs.a: ಪಟ್ಟಿ (lists): shopping lists, word lists, daily plans. Lists forgive grammar, demand spelling, and get used — the perfect beginner writing.
faqs.q: What should I write first?

faqs.a: ಪತ್ರ (letters) to friends, ಟಿಪ್ಪಣಿ (notes) to self, ಮನೆಕೆಲಸ (homework) for courses. Real writing to real readers beats copied exercises every time.
faqs.q: When real writing?

topics.lede: Letters to lists to letters — writing from first strokes to full pages.
topics.note: A note on ಸಹಿ. Your ಸಹಿ (signature) in Kannada script is a milestone — practise it until it flows in one confident motion. Signing Kannada-style on forms, cards and letters declares belonging more than any certificate.
paras: Writing starts with strokes: Kannada letters curve and loop — ಬರೆಯಿರಿ (please write) circles, hooks and waves before full letters. Trace ಅ ಆ ಇ ಈ ಉ ಊ big and slow; the hand learns shapes the eye already knows.
Tools matter little, mileage matters all: ಲೇಖನಿ (pen), pencil, finger on steamed mirrors — Kannada children trace in rice, sand and air. Write everywhere; medium is vanity, motion is learning.

Lists graduate the hand: ಪಟ್ಟಿ (list) — ಟಿಪ್ಪಣಿ (notes), ವಿಳಾಸ (addresses), ದಿನಾಂಕ (dates). Copy your own ಹೆಸರು (name) fifty times, then friends' names, then street names. Familiar words, fresh script: the fastest fluent hand.

Real writing arrives: ಪತ್ರ (letters), ಅರ್ಜಿ (applications), ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ (exams), ಮನೆಕೆಲಸ (homework). Write a postcard to yourself in Kannada — short, joyful, posted. First posted Kannada is never forgotten.
topics.title: Writing Kannada

topics.desc: Who does what, verb last — Kannada sentences decoded with living examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Subject-Object-Verb: ನಾನು ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಓದುತ್ತೇನೆ (I book read). Endings mark roles, so order flexes for emphasis — but verb-last is home.
faqs.q: What is Kannada word order?

faqs.a: Tense lives on the verb: ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ (go-present), ಹೋದೆ (went), ಹೋಗುವೆ. Time words — ನಿನ್ನೆ, ಇಂದು, ನಾಳೆ — frame it; the verb carries it.
faqs.q: How do tenses work?

faqs.a: Add -ಆ and rise: ಅದು ನಿನ್ನ ಪುಸ್ತಕನಾ? (is that your book?). Question words — ಏನು, ಎಲ್ಲಿ, ಯಾರು — sit where the answer would.
faqs.q: How do I ask questions?

topics.lede: Who does what, verb last — sentences decoded with living examples.
topics.note: A note on ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತಿದೆ. Kannada weather does things: ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತಿದೆ (rain comes), ಬಿಸಿಲು ಹೊಡೆಯುತ್ತಿದೆ (sun strikes), ಗಾಳಿ ಬೀಸುತ್ತಿದೆ (wind blows). No empty it — Kannada skies act. Weather sentences teach SOV with zero confusion: subject, then verb, done.
paras: Simple sentences stack three blocks: ನಾನು ಶಾಲೆಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ (I — to-school — go), ಅವಳು ಹಾಡು ಹಾಡುತ್ತಾಳೆ (she — song — sings), ನಾವು ಕನ್ನಡ ಓದುತ್ತೇವೆ (we — Kannada — study). Subject, object, verb — build a hundred of these and Kannada skeleton is yours.

Animals make perfect practice: ಹುಡುಗ ನಗುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾನೆ (the boy laughs), ನಾಯಿ ಬೊಗಳುತ್ತಿದೆ (the dog barks), ಬೆಕ್ಕು ಮಲಗಿದೆ (the cat sleeps). Short subjects, vivid verbs, zero ambiguity — describe every creature you meet and SOV becomes reflex.

Time flexes the frame: ನಾನು ನಾಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ (I'll come tomorrow), ನಿನ್ನೆ ಮಳೆ ಬಂತು (it rained yesterday). Time words float — front for emphasis, middle for flow — while the verb holds the end. Tense plus time word: past, present, future, mastered.

Identity and questions close the set: ಇದು ನನ್ನ ಮನೆ (this is my house), ಅದು ನಿನ್ನ ಪುಸ್ತಕನಾ? (is that your book?), ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದೆ (all is well). Equate with ಇದು/ಅದು, question with -ಆ, reassure with ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದೆ — sentences for every situation.
topics.title: Kannada sentence structure

topics.desc: Rahul becomes ರಾಹುಲ್ — spell, write and own your name in Kannada script. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Sound it out in Kannada letters: Rahul → ರಾಹುಲ್, Priya → ಪ್ರಿಯಾ, John → ಜಾನ್. Kannada spells by ear — say your name slowly, catch each sound, write each letter.
faqs.q: How do I write my name in Kannada?

faqs.a: Loan letters — ಜ (ja), ಹ (ha), ಶ ಷ ಸ (sha/sa) — handle foreign sounds. ಜಾನ್ (John), ಹೋಟೆಲ್ (hotel) — borrowed letters for borrowed names, fully Kannada now.
faqs.q: What about sounds Kannada lacks?

faqs.a: ಮೊದಲ ಅಕ್ಷರ (first letter) starts it, ಕೊನೆಯ ಅಕ್ಷರ (last letter) ends it. Introduce with ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು... (my name is...), then write it — introductions stick twice as well written.
faqs.q: How do I introduce my name?

topics.lede: Rahul becomes ರಾಹುಲ್ — spell, write and own your name in Kannada.
topics.note: A note on ರಾಹುಲ್. Foreign names glide in Kannada script — Rahul appears as ರಾಹುಲ್ with a soft ಹ, sometimes ರಾವುಲ್. All are read Rahul; none is wrong. Kannada welcomes foreign names with flexible spelling — pick the shape you love and own it.
paras: Names transliterate by ear: break yours into sounds, match each to Kannada letters — ರವಿ (Ravi), ಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಿ (Lakshmi), ಕಿರಣ್ (Kiran) show the pattern. Say it slow, write it true — ಸ್ಪೆಲ್ಲಿಂಗ್ (spelling) by sound, not by English letters.
Foreign sounds borrow loan letters: ಜ for John (ಜಾನ್), ಹ for hotels and Rahuls, ಶ for Sharma sounds. These Sanskrit-born letters are Kannada citizens now — use them proudly for every imported sound.

Introductions pair speech and script: ಪರಿಚಯ (introduction) — ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು... (my name is...), spoken, then written. ಹೆಸರು ಫಲಕಗಳು (name boards) on doors and desks teach daily — read every board, collect every name.

Nicknames warm everything: ಅಡ್ಡಹೆಸರು (nickname) — ಚಿನ್ನು (gold/darling), ಕಣೋ (dear), ಪುಟ್ಟ (little one). Kannada shortens with love: Ravi becomes ರವಿ, Lakshmi becomes ಲಚ್ಚು. Earn a Kannada nickname and you have arrived.
topics.title: Write your name in Kannada

topics.desc: ಸಖತ್, ಮಚ್ಚಾ, ಬೇರೆ ಲೆವೆಲ್ — street Kannada that films, friends and fun run on. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ಸೂಪರ್ (super) and ಸಖತ್ (awesome) — positive, universal, safe. Sprinkle them on food, films and friends; instant insider status.
faqs.q: What slang is safe everywhere?

faqs.a: ಮಚ್ಚಾ (dude) and ಗುರು (guru/dude) — for friends only, never elders or strangers. Friendship slang misused offends; rightly used, it bonds instantly.
faqs.q: Can I call people machchaa?

faqs.a: ಸುಮ್ನೆ (just like that / for fun) — ಸುಮ್ನೆ ಹೇಳ್ದೆ (just kidding), ಸುಮ್ನೆ ಬಂದೆ (just dropped by). The most Kannada word in existence: purposeless joy, declared proudly.
faqs.q: What does sumne mean?

topics.lede: ಸಖತ್, ಮಚ್ಚಾ, ಬೇರೆ ಲೆವೆಲ್ — street Kannada that fun runs on.
topics.note: A note on ಸುಮ್ನೆ. ಸುಮ್ನೆ (sumne) defies translation — just because, for fun, no reason, chill. ಏಕೆ? — ಸುಮ್ನೆ (why? — just because). Whole philosophies hide in two syllables; use it freely, smile always.
paras: Praise slang opens doors: ಸೂಪರ್ (super), ಸಖತ್ (awesome), ಬೇರೆ ಲೆವೆಲ್ (next level), ಮಜಾ (fun/great), ಅಬ್ಬಾ (wow). Food, films, friends' outfits — praise everything loudly. Kannada people praise generously; learners should too.

Friendship words bond crews: ಮಚ್ಚಾ (dude), ಗುರು (guru/dude), ಭಾಯ್ (bro) — friends-only, always warm. ಮಚ್ಚಾ ಬಾ (come on dude) starts a thousand conversations daily. Never aim them upward at elders; sideways at friends, fire freely.

Reaction words colour stories: ಅಯ್ಯೋ (oh no!), ಅಬ್ಬಾ (wow!), ಕತೆ ಹೇಳ್ಬೇಡ (stop making things up!). Kannada storytelling runs on reactions — gasp, laugh, disbelieve theatrically. Flat faces kill stories; big reactions feed them.

Playful edges season everything: ಹೋಗೋ (get lost — playful among friends, rude otherwise), ಛೇ (mild disgust), ಸುಮ್ನೆ (just because). Learn the edges, respect the edges: slang's power is knowing exactly where fun ends.
topics.title: Kannada slang

topics.desc: Toys, moons, stars and good-child gold — Kannada for little learners, big joy. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Songs and ಕತೆ (stories) — ಹಾಡು with actions, tales with voices. Children absorb Kannada through music and play long before grammar.
faqs.q: How do kids learn Kannada best?

faqs.a: ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಹುಡುಗ / ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಹುಡುಗಿ (good boy / good girl) — praise every attempt loudly. Kannada parenting runs on encouragement; learners of all ages bloom under it.
faqs.q: How do I praise a child?

faqs.a: ಆಟ (games): name objects — ಚೆಂಡು! ಗೊಂಬೆ! — count steps, sing counts. Play first, words hitchhike.
faqs.q: Games or lessons?

topics.lede: Toys, moons, stars and gold stars — Kannada for little learners, big joy.
topics.note: A note on ಚಿನ್ನು. ಚಿನ್ನು (chinnu — gold/darling) melts every Kannada heart — ನನ್ನ ಚಿನ್ನು (my darling) for children, pets and beloveds. Terms of endearment are Kannada's mother tongue; every child swims in them.
paras: Little learners start with love: ಮಕ್ಕಳು (children), ಪಾಪು (baby), ಚಿನ್ನು (darling), ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಹುಡುಗ (good boy). Kannada childhood floats on affection-words — call every child ಚಿನ್ನು and watch faces light like ದೀಪಾವಳಿ.
Play teaches fastest: ಆಟ (play), ಗೊಂಬೆ (toy), ಚೆಂಡು (ball) — ಆಡೋಣ (let's play)! Count throws, name colours, chase and giggle. Play first; Kannada hitchhikes on joy.
School words structure days: ಶಾಲೆ (school), ಉಪಾಧ್ಯಾಯ (teacher), ಪಾಠ (lesson), ಮನೆಕೆಲಸ (homework). ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ ಟೀಚರ್ (hello teacher) opens every school day — respect and learning, hand in hand.

Sky words spark wonder: ಸೂರ್ಯ (sun), ಚಂದಮಾಮ (moon), ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ (star) — ಚಂದಮಾಮ ನೋಡು (look at the moon)! Night-sky Kannada, whispered on terraces, becomes lifelong memory. Teach the sky; the child keeps the language.
topics.title: Kannada for kids

topics.desc: Meetings, customers, contracts — professional Kannada for offices and business. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ, ನಾನು... (hello, I'm...) — then ನಿಮ್ಮನ್ನು ಭೇಟಿಯಾಗಿದ್ದು ಸಂತೋಷ (pleased to meet you). Business Kannada opens formal and warms slowly.
faqs.q: How do I introduce myself at work?

faqs.a: ಸಭೆ ಯಾವಾಗ? (when is the meeting?) and ಸಭೆ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? (where?). Meetings run Kannada offices — never miss one for language reasons.
faqs.q: How do I ask about meetings?

faqs.a: ಈಮೇಲ್ ಕಳಿಸುತ್ತೇನೆ (I'll send an email) and ಫೋನಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತಾಡೋಣ (let's talk on the phone). Digital Kannada borrows freely — clarity beats purity in business.
faqs.q: Email and phone in Kannada?

topics.lede: Meetings, customers, contracts — professional Kannada for offices.
topics.note: A note on ಗ್ರಾಹಕ. ಗ್ರಾಹಕ (graahaka — customer) rules Kannada business — pure, proud, universal. It takes practice to say smoothly (graa-ha-ka); clients notice the effort and reward it. Master it syllable by syllable.
paras: Workplaces run on roles: ಕೆಲಸ (work/job), ಆಫೀಸು (office), ಬಾಸ್ (boss), ಗ್ರಾಹಕ (customer), ಸಹೋದ್ಯೋಗಿ (colleague). ನನ್ನ ಕೆಲಸ... (my work is...) introduces your profession; ಆಫೀಸು ಎಲ್ಲಿ? finds any office. Roles first, tasks second.

Meetings move business: ಸಭೆ (meeting), ಒಪ್ಪಂದ (contract/deal), ಸಹಿ (signature). ಸಭೆ ನಾಳೆ ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ (meeting tomorrow morning) — confirm with ಸರಿ, ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ (okay, I'll come). Kannada meetings open with ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ and close with ಧನ್ಯವಾದ.
Money talks plainly: ಲಾಭ (profit), ನಷ್ಟ (loss), ಸಂಬಳ (salary), ರಜೆ (leave). ಸಂಬಳ ಯಾವಾಗ? (when is payday?) — asked smiling, everywhere. Business Kannada respects directness wrapped in politeness.
Digital tools connect all: ಈಮೇಲ್ (email), ಫೋನ್ (phone), ಮೆಸೇಜ್ (message). ಈಮೇಲ್ ನೋಡಿ (please check email) — then ಯಶಸ್ಸು (success) follows effort. Professional Kannada: formal words, warm heart.
topics.title: Kannada for work and business

topics.desc: Kuvempu, temples, Dasara — reclaim the Kannada your family carried. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Start with sounds you half-know: family words, food names, festival greetings. Heritage ears remember more than they admit — recognition unlocks fast, then production follows.
faqs.q: I understand but can't speak — help?

faqs.a: ಕುವೆಂಪು (Kuvempu) — poet laureate, Jnanpith winner, voice of Karnataka. Learn one stanza by heart; Kannada people of every age will beam.
faqs.q: What is the one classic to know?

faqs.a: ದಸರಾ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು (Dasara greetings) and ಯುಗಾದಿ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು (Ugadi greetings) — festivals are heritage made annual. Greet first, belong instantly.
faqs.q: Festival greetings?

topics.lede: Kuvempu, temples, Dasara — reclaim the Kannada your family carried.
topics.note: A note on ಮಾತೃಭಾಷೆ. ಮಾತೃಭಾಷೆ (maatru-bhaashe — mother tongue) is Kannada's most emotional word — language as mother. ನನ್ನ ಮಾತೃಭಾಷೆ ಕನ್ನಡ (my mother tongue is Kannada) is identity declared. Heritage learners don't study Kannada; they come home to it.
paras: Heritage starts with recognition: ಪರಂಪರೆ (heritage), ಪೂರ್ವಜರು (ancestors), ಮಾತೃಭಾಷೆ (mother tongue), ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಿ (culture). Words you heard at knees and kitchens — say them now deliberately. Passive memory converts to active speech within weeks of trying.

Temples anchor memory: ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನ (temple), ಹಬ್ಬ (festival), ಪೂಜೆ (worship). Every heritage family carries temple Kannada — bell-sounds, flower-names, prayer-lines. Revisit a ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನ with learning ears; childhood vocabulary resurfaces like monsoon wells.

Festivals calendar the year: ದಸರಾ (victory, autumn — Mysuru's glory), ಯುಗಾದಿ (New Year, spring), ದೀಪಾವಳಿ (lights). Festival kitchens teach fastest — grind, stir, taste, name everything. Heritage you can eat stays learned.

Classics crown the journey: ಕುವೆಂಪು (Kuvempu's verse), ಪುರಂದರದಾಸ (Purandaradasa's songs), ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು to ಮೈಸೂರು — ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ entire. One stanza memorised outweighs ten lessons completed; heritage learners carry literature, not just language.
topics.title: Kannada for heritage learners

topics.desc: Weeks to chat, months to flow, a year to shine — honest timelines, faster methods. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Survival in 2–4 weeks (greetings, numbers, food), conversation in 3–6 months, comfort in a year — at 20 minutes daily. Consistency beats intensity every time.
faqs.q: How long to hold a conversation?

faqs.a: ಳ, the three sibilants, verb-final order, ನನಗೆ-style wanting. Each surrenders to weeks of drilling — this track attacks every one directly.
faqs.q: What takes longest in Kannada?

faqs.a: Daily contact plus weekly speaking: ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ಅಭ್ಯಾಸ (practise daily), ವಾರ ಮಾತಾಡಿ (speak weekly). Apps maintain; conversations advance.
faqs.q: What speeds learning most?

topics.lede: Weeks to chat, months to flow, a year to shine — honest timelines.
topics.note: A note on ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ. ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ (pratidina — daily, every day) is the whole secret — ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ (a little every day) beats weekend marathons completely. Streaks compound; Kannada rewards the faithful, not the frantic.
paras: Levels ladder clearly: ಆರಂಭಿಕ ಹಂತ (beginner — weeks 1–8: survival phrases, core sounds), ಮಧ್ಯಮ ಹಂತ (intermediate — months 3–8: conversations, tenses, reading), ಉನ್ನತ ಹಂತ (advanced — month 9+: films, debates, literature). Each ಹಂತ (level) feels impossible until suddenly it doesn't.

Habits beat hours: ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ (daily) contact, ಅಭ್ಯಾಸ (habit) over heroics. Fifteen minutes of ದಿನವೂ practice — five words, one dialogue, one song line — compounds to fluency while motivation merely visits. Streaks are sacred; protect yours.

Goals steer progress: ಗುರಿ (goal) — ಪ್ರಾರಂಭ (start) with survival, ಪ್ರಗತಿ (progress) monthly measured. This month: order food. Next: small talk. Then: phone calls. Concrete ಗುರಿ, celebrated loudly — ಸರಳತೆ (fluency) is a trail of kept promises.

Mastery crowns patience: ಪರಿಣತಿ (mastery), ಛಲ (persistence), ವಿಶ್ವಾಸ (confidence). A year of faithful days buys comfortable conversation; two buys belonging. Kannada has waited fifteen centuries — it will wait for you, and reward you richly.
topics.title: How long does Kannada take?

topics.desc: Dravidian roots, Sanskrit friends, Hindi neighbours — Kannada's place in India's language family. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Distant cousins — Kannada is Dravidian; Hindi, Bengali and Marathi are Indo-Aryan. Shared nation, shared Sanskrit loans, different grandmothers.
faqs.q: Is Kannada related to Hindi?

faqs.a: ತೆಲುಗು — the closest sibling, neighbours for a thousand years, scripts that look like twins. The kannada-vs-telugu page maps both.
faqs.q: Which language is closest to Kannada?

faqs.a: Centuries of poetry, prayer and scholarship — ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತ words fill formal Kannada while grammar stays purely Dravidian. Sanskrit lends vocabulary; Kannada keeps its soul.
faqs.q: Why so much Sanskrit in Kannada?

topics.lede: Dravidian roots, Sanskrit friends, Hindi neighbours — Kannada's family place.
topics.note: A note on ದ್ರಾವಿಡ. ದ್ರಾವಿಡ (Dravidian) names one of the world's great language families — Kannada its classical-crowned child, with eight Jnanpiths and fifteen centuries of writing. Dravidian pride runs deep and joyful; learners inherit the celebration.
paras: Kannada anchors the Dravidian west: ತೆಲುಗು (Telugu), ತಮಿಳು (Tamil), ಮಲಯಾಳಂ (Malayalam) — siblings, not dialects. Shared grammar bones, shared ancient words, four proud literatures. Learn Kannada and Telugu signboards start whispering.

The north speaks Indo-Aryan: ಹಿಂದಿ (Hindi), ಬಂಗಾಳಿ (Bengali), ಮರಾಠಿ (Marathi), ಗುಜರಾತಿ (Gujarati), ಪಂಜಾಬಿ (Punjabi) — Sanskrit-descended cousins. Different family, shared nation: ಭಾರತ (India) holds both, and ಅನುವಾದ (translation) bridges all.

Sanskrit threads everything: ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತ lent Kannada thousands of formal words. Pure-Kannada movements coin Dravidian replacements; daily speech mixes happily. Both registers are real Kannada; learners need both.

Unity crowns diversity: ಏಕತೆ (unity) — 22 official languages, hundreds of mother tongues, one conversation. Kannada people learn Hindi for Delhi, English for globe, Kannada for soul. Every Indian language you meet makes your Kannada richer.
topics.title: Kannada among Indian languages

topics.desc: Twin scripts, sibling sounds — Kannada and Telugu, neighbours for 1000 years. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Scripts read similarly — ಅಮ್ಮ/అమ్మ, similar letter-shapes everywhere. Speech differs more: shared roots, drifted sounds. Learn one script, peek into both.
faqs.q: Are the scripts really alike?

faqs.a: Hundreds: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ/నమస్కారం, ಅಮ್ಮ/అమ్మ, similar numbers, matching grammar. Core vocabulary overlaps enormously; learn one list, own two hearts.
faqs.q: How many words are shared?

faqs.a: Kannada first for structure, Telugu ears second for music. Each language halves the other's difficulty — learn one, get the second at a discount.
faqs.q: Which should I learn first?

topics.lede: Twin scripts, sibling sounds — neighbours for 1000 years.
topics.note: A note on ಅಮ್ಮ = అమ్మ. Kannada ಅಮ್ಮ (mother) and Telugu అమ్మ are the SAME ancient word in twin scripts — hundreds work this way. Learn Kannada's core well and Telugu signboards start reading themselves.
paras: The siblings grew side by side: ಕನ್ನಡ west in ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ, తెలుగు (Telugu) east in Andhra-Telangana. Same Dravidian mother — verb-final grammar, -ಗೆ/-కు wanting, elder-younger siblings — and scripts so alike that learners mix them for weeks.
Shared words delight learners: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ/నమస్కారం (hello), ಅಮ್ಮ/అమ్మ (mother), similar pronouns, matching numbers. Core vocabulary overlaps enormously; learn one list, own two languages' hearts.

Split sounds mark the border: Kannada ನಾನು against Telugu నేను (I), ನೀವು against మీరు, ಹೌದು against అవును. Pronouns and yes-no drifted most — precisely the words learners say most. Drill the pairs; cross the border daily.

Scripts twin but speech parts: ಕನ್ನಡ ಲಿಪಿ and తెలుగు లిపి share letter-shapes and ottakshara logic — yet a Kannada film needs subtitles in Hyderabad. Sisters recognise sisters on paper; ears take longer. Learn either with love and both reward you.
topics.title: Kannada vs Telugu

topics.desc: Dialogues, songs and power-star speeches — learn Kannada the Sandalwood way. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Comedies and romances — clear speech, everyday words, repeatable ಡೈಲಾಗ್ (dialogues). Action films thrill but mumble; ಪ್ರೀತಿ (romance) teaches.
faqs.q: Which films teach best?

faqs.a: Watch once with subtitles for story, again pausing to shadow dialogues, songs on loop for sounds. Three passes per film: story, speech, song.
faqs.q: How do I learn from films?

faqs.a: Start with famous lines — short, dramatic, unforgettable. Film dialogues stick like songs; mimicry is fluency's shortcut.
faqs.q: Film dialogues or songs first?

topics.lede: Dialogues, songs and power-star speeches — Kannada the Sandalwood way.
topics.note: A note on ಪವರ್ ಸ್ಟಾರ್. ಪವರ್ ಸ್ಟಾರ್ (Power Star) means one beloved man in Karnataka: Puneeth Rajkumar, forever Appu. Film love here is devotion — first-day-first-show crowds, cutouts garlanded like gods. Learn Kannada and you inherit the celebration.
paras: Cinema is Kannada's second classroom: ಸಿನಿಮಾ (cinema), ಥಿಯೇಟರ್ (theatre), ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ (release) — Friday releases are festivals. ನಟ (actors) and ನಟಿ (actresses) are family members; ನಿರ್ದೇಶಕ (directors) are debated like philosophers. Watch and belong.

Genres teach registers: ಪ್ರೀತಿ (romance) speaks softly, ಹಾಸ್ಯ (comedy) snaps jokes, ಆಕ್ಷನ್ (action) barks orders. Romance first — gentle pace, tender words; comedy second — speed and slang; action last — glory without subtlety.

Dialogues drill memory: ಡೈಲಾಗ್ (dialogue) — repeat famous lines until they own you. Kannada mass dialogues are poetry with punch; delivering one correctly earns applause from auto drivers to executives. Shadow the stars shamelessly.

Music melts resistance: ಸಂಗೀತ (music), ಹಾಡು (songs) — learn lyrics line by line, sing them wrong then right. ಅಭಿಮಾನಿ (fans) sing together; join them. Cinema Kannada is joyful Kannada — and joyful Kannada sticks forever.
topics.title: Learning from Kannada cinema

topics.desc: Friends, lovers, weddings — the Kannada of hearts, spoken truly. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ (male friend), ಸ್ನೇಹಿತೆ (female friend) — then ಅನುರಾಗ (love) and ವಾತ್ಸಲ್ಯ (affection) as bonds deepen. Friendship words first; romance follows naturally.
faqs.q: Friendship words first?

faqs.a: ಮದುವೆ (spoken wedding), ವಿವಾಹ (formal wedding) — ಮದುಮಗ (groom), ಮದುಮಗಳು (bride). ಮದುವೆ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು (wedding greetings) blesses every couple.
faqs.q: How do I talk about weddings?

faqs.a: ಕ್ಷಮೆ (forgiveness) — ನನ್ನನ್ನು ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ (please forgive me), then ಸಂಧಾನ (peace). Kannada reconciliations run deep and warm; ask sincerely, receive fully.
faqs.q: How do I apologise deeply?

topics.lede: Friends, lovers, weddings — the Kannada of hearts, spoken truly.
topics.note: A note on ಪ್ರೀತಿ vs ಅನುರಾಗ. ಪ್ರೀತಿ (preeti) is romance specifically; ಅನುರಾಗ (anuraaga) is broad love — family, friends, humanity. ನಿಮ್ಮ ಅನುರಾಗಕ್ಕೆ ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (thanks for your love) suits everyone; ಪ್ರೀತಿ belongs to one. Kannada loves precisely.
paras: Friendship opens hearts: ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ (male friend), ಸ್ನೇಹಿತೆ (female friend) — ನನ್ನ ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ (my friend) introduces proudly. Kannada friendships run lifelong and deep; ಸ್ನೇಹ (friendship) is celebrated in poetry, films and daily tea. Make one Kannada friend and gain a hundred phrases.

Romance speaks softly: ಪ್ರಿಯಕರ (boyfriend), ಪ್ರಿಯತಮೆ (girlfriend), ಪ್ರೀತಿ (love). Kannada romance favours poetry over bluntness — film songs teach the register better than textbooks. Learn gently; speak truly.

Weddings unite families: ಮದುವೆ (wedding spoken), ವಿವಾಹ (wedding formal), ಮದುಮಗ (groom), ಮದುಮಗಳು (bride). Kannada weddings run for days — music, food, rituals, blessings. ಮದುವೆ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು (wedding congratulations) is your ticket to the feast.

Bonds deepen and mend: ಅನುರಾಗ (love), ವಾತ್ಸಲ್ಯ (affection), ಜೀವನ (life) — ನನ್ನ ಜೀವನ (my life) means my beloved. And when bonds strain: ಕ್ಷಮೆ (forgiveness), ಸಂಧಾನ (peace). Kannada hearts forgive spaciously; ask with folded hands.
topics.title: Talking about relationships

topics.desc: Spaced repetition, topic decks, daily streaks — flashcards that actually work. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ಮತ್ತೆ ಮತ್ತೆ (again and again) — but spaced: 1 day, 3 days, 7 days, 30 days. ಅಂತರ (spacing) beats cramming; ನೆನಪು (memory) loves intervals.
faqs.q: How often should I review?

faqs.a: Five to ten per topic — quality over quantity. Master one ಕಾರ್ಡ್ deck fully before opening the next; half-known decks rot.
faqs.q: How many cards per topic?

faqs.a: ದಿನವೂ (daily) short sessions — ten minutes, every day, no exceptions. Streaks compound; ಮರೆವು (forgetting) loses to routine.
faqs.q: Daily or weekly review?

topics.lede: Spaced repetition, topic decks, daily streaks — flashcards that work.
topics.note: A note on ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ (punaraavartane — revision, repeating-again) is Kannada's own word for spaced review — recalling again, and again, at widening intervals. The language itself teaches the method: revisit, widen, remember.
paras: Cards carry memory: ಕಾರ್ಡ್ (card) — one word, one side; meaning, the other. ನೆನಪು (memory) strengthens with every recall; ಮರೆವು (forgetting) is just unreviewed memory. Build decks per topic — greetings, food, verbs — and review each separately.

Spacing schedules success: ಅಂತರ (interval) — review new cards tomorrow, then in three days, seven, thirty. ಮತ್ತೆ ಮತ್ತೆ (again and again), but wider each time. Cramming fills hours; spacing fills years.

Rhythms sustain streaks: ದಿನವೂ (daily) quick decks, ವಾರಕ್ಕೊಮ್ಮೆ (weekly) full reviews, ತಿಂಗಳಿಗೊಮ್ಮೆ (monthly) championships. Ten daily minutes beat Sunday marathons; streaks turn study into ಅಭ್ಯಾಸ (habit).

Scores gamify growth: ಅಂಕಗಳು (marks), ಸ್ಪರ್ಧೆ (contest), ಗೆಲುವು (victory) — even ಸೋಲು (defeat) teaches. Quiz yourself, beat yesterday's score, celebrate loudly. Flashcards are games that pay in fluency.
topics.title: Flashcards by topic
